name: Columbia Gas Transmission Virginia Reliability Project
researcher_notes: EIA August 2026 release, sheet 'Historical Projects (1996-2024)', Excel row 1203 (name Virginia Reliability Project, docket CP22-503): Completed, in service 2025 (commercial service November 2025), 49 miles, 24 inch, 100 MMcf/d additional capacity, cost 500 million USD, Columbia Gas Transmission (TC Energy), Virginia only. World Pipelines (Nov 2023) states FERC approval and about 48 miles of 1950s 12 inch replaced by 24 inch, owned by TC Energy. WHRO (July 2024) says about 49 miles replaced and widened, ending in Suffolk and Chesapeake, construction begun. FERC final environmental impact statement exists for the project. Not an existing row: P2516 (Central Virginia Connector, 0 km) and P4446 (Virginia Electrification) are different projects. Passes the add threshold: sponsor, endpoints, FERC certificate, built; 49 mi (about 79 km) of new 24 inch pipe is well above 25 km. It replaces old 12 inch pipe, but the 24 inch line is new steel pipe and EIA counts it as 49 miles, so staged as an expansion row under parent Columbia Gas Transmission. Replacement of the old line is a judgment call for Baird. EIA is one origin; World Pipelines and WHRO give independent length and status context but only EIA states in-service. Status-by-completion rests on EIA alone, so tier medium. Start location is not stated in the sources (reports say Sussex or Surry County, or Petersburg and Emporia area), so left blank. Route not found; official FERC GIS shapefile not retrieved. Capacity 100 MMcf/d is incremental, matching 100,000 Dth/d in the project notes. Owner spelled per gazetteer hit Columbia Gas Transmission LLC. The order of Start/End cannot be confirmed. Parent not staged.
